chapters.title: Getting Your Bearings
chapters.intro: Before the history, the ground rules: how this book weighs evidence, where the places in the story are, who the Palestinians are in law today, who may become a citizen of Israel, and what the most argued-over legal words actually mean.

sections.brief: How the book grades evidence (documented, reported, contested, unresolved), uses both sides' official records, labels advocacy, and says who made it. Then the method for a viral claim from cmt_s01: a true fact attached to a conclusion it does not support. Embed claim_checker:How to Check:0 and walk through its three questions. Close with the standard applied to this project itself.

The map: Israel within the 1949 Green Line, the West Bank and Oslo II's Areas A (about 18%), B (about 22%) and C (about 61%), Gaza, and East Jerusalem, with every figure and the four legal regimes. From sk_s07, tell how East Jerusalem's status was set: the 1980 Basic Law, Security Council Resolution 478 (14–0, US abstaining), embassies leaving by 2006 and the US embassy opening on 14 May 2018. Present Israel's position and the UN's side by side. Figure: a comparison table of the four places and who governs each.

Who the Palestinians are in law: about 14.8 million worldwide (PCBS 2024), in four legal situations, with 5.9 million registered refugees. For citizens of Israel, use population_now's end-2023 figures (Arabs 21.3% of 9.7 million; Jerusalem 39.9% Arab) and compare 1967. Tell briefly from mg_s01 the military government over Arab citizens (1949–1966) and Kafr Qasim, and from nsl_s01 the 2018 Nation-State Law (62–55, upheld 10–1) and Arabic's 'special status', linking forward. Figures: key figures; a comparison of the four legal situations. Make clear why the 'apartheid' argument turns on these differences, and leave the legal finding to pr_s03.

Who may become a citizen of Israel, from the primary texts: the Law of Return (5 July 1950), its 1954 and 1970 amendments (the grandchild clause and the definition of a Jew), and the Nationality Law of 1952, whose residence conditions decided which Arabs who stayed in 1948 became citizens. Then the 2003 family-unification ban: the court rulings of 2006 (6–5) and 2012, its lapse in July 2021 and its re-enactment on 10 March 2022 (45–15). Present both disputes fairly: refuge law against discriminatory law, including Joppke and Rosenhek's comparison with Germany; and security against demography, with Shin Bet's numbers and the 2022 text's own wording. Figures: a timeline of the laws; a comparison of the paths to citizenship by return and by residence. Link the Absentees' Property Law forward [scene:ap_s01].

What 'occupation', 'apartheid' and 'genocide' mean in law, who has found what (a court, a UN body, NGOs, governments), and Israel's rejection of each finding. Tell briefly from icj_s01 what the ICJ advised on 19 July 2024, and from sk_s02 what the democracy indices measure and whom they leave out (V-Dem's 2024 downgrade). Embed gaza_record:The Law:0 and gaza_record:The Law:1 and discuss their dates and Israel's stated position. State plainly that the genocide case is undecided. Figure: a comparison of the three terms by legal source, who found it, and who disputes it.

chapters.title: The Land Before the State
chapters.intro: Three thousand years in brief: what the stones and the ancient writers name, the Ottoman province that was counted and governed, the Jewish community that lived there before Zionism, and two peoples whose histories in this land are both real.

sections.brief: From the Merneptah stele (c. 1207 BCE: Israel as a people), the Tel Dan and Mesha stelae (c. 840 BCE) and the kingdoms of Israel and Judah, through Rome (63 BCE, 70 CE, Bar Kokhba 132–135/136, Syria Palaestina) and the Jewish presence that remained, to Byzantine, Muslim (Jund Filastin), Crusader, Mamluk and Ottoman rule, with the history of the name 'Palestine' from Herodotus on. Present the dispute over Hadrian's motive (Feldman against Syme and Jacobson) and Bowersock's critique of Masalha's continuity claim, and use cmt_s07's verdict on the 'name stolen from Rome' claim. Figure: a timeline of rulers and names, at most 7 rows.

Ottoman Palestine as an administered place: the Mutasarrifate of Jerusalem reporting directly to Constantinople from 1872, the three districts, about 600,000 people and the named cities, with the honest technical point that no province was called 'Palestine'. Add the wider Ottoman order from me_s01 (millets, no hard borders), imperial rule rather than settler colonization from tk_s01 (ending with Lausanne, 1923), and the state of things before 1948 from iaa_s03; mention the 1858 Land Code only in a phrase and link [scene:ot_s01]. Embed map me_layers. Figure: a power structure of Ottoman administration (Sultan, Mutasarrifate, sanjaks).

The Jewish community before Zionism: the Old Yishuv, the four holy cities, halukka and its kollels, the Ottoman-recognized Sephardi chief rabbi, and the numbers with sources and ranges (about 7,000 Jews in 1800; 23,000–27,000 in 1880; McCarthy's Ottoman-citizen counts, which exclude foreign nationals). Present the Jerusalem-majority dispute: Israel's UN letter S/10138 (1887–1944 figures) against Jordan's sub-district figures, plus Flatow and Frantzman, noting the conflicting 1922 city totals (62,578 against 52,081). Embed prestate_funding:People:0 and discuss its 11%, 17% and 33% shares as the continuation under the Mandate. Figures: key figures; a comparison of the city figures with the Ottoman-register figures. Link the First Aliyah forward [scene:ideo_s01].

Three separate questions, kept separate: population presence (the 1871–72 census: 381,954 people, about 85% Muslim, 11% Christian, 4% Jewish), cultural continuity, and modern national identity, which is modern on both sides (Khalidi's finding for Palestinians; Basel 1897 for Zionism). Use cmt_s06's evidence (Filastin, 1911; the congresses from 1919; the 1922 census of 757,182) against the 'invented in the 1960s' claim, and sq_s05 on 'a land without a people' (1843; first Zionist use 1901) and the 'two-thousand-year war'. Embed prestate_funding:People:1 and discuss its figures. State the strongest form of each side's claim to indigeneity, and link forward to the newspaper [scene:fil_s01].

chapters.title: Words and Names
chapters.intro: What the name 'Israel' says in its first text, and one labeled reading of it; where 'Semitic' and 'antisemitism' came from, and the hatred that is older than the word; what the flag's symbol records; and how the word is now used, and argued over, as a shield.

sections.brief: Genesis 32:22–32 from the text: Jacob's night of wrestling, the renaming at 32:28, the root (El plus sarah, 'strives with God') and its two valid readings, and the crooked-heel wordplay. Then the layers added later: a people, a land, and in 1948 a state. Use every occurrence count and parallel confirmation in the deep dives. In one sentence, link back to the Merneptah stele as the first outside mention [scene:ah_s01].

A clearly labeled interpretive passage, not a finding: the IS–RA–EL reading as symbolic resonance, where it stops, and the one piece of it that is real etymology (El). Ground it in the traditions' own named methods of non-literal reading: PaRDeS, ta'wil, and Origen and the medieval Catholic four senses. Open and close the section by saying plainly that this is a reading. Figure: a comparison of the documentary etymology and the symbolic reading.

Shem and the Genesis genealogy as the root; Schlözer's language family (Hebrew, Aramaic, Arabic, Amharic, Maltese); Palestinian Arabs as a Semitic-speaking people of the same ancient Levantine population, with the genetic evidence. Mention Marr in a phrase and leave his story to s00b0, and leave IHRA and the Jerusalem Declaration to s00b1. Keep the named critics of the Jerusalem Declaration in this section's dispute so the other side is heard where the 'swizzle' is first named. Figure: a family tree of the Semitic languages as a power-structure figure.

Antisemitism as a hatred, named plainly, before and after the word: the blood libel from Norwich (1144) to Trent (1475, repudiated in 1965); the Lateran badge decree (1215), England's badge (1218), the Statute of Jewry (1275), the expulsion of 1290 and readmission in 1656; Damascus 1840 (the friar's disappearance, torture, Montefiore and Crémieux, the Sultan's firman); Kishinev 1903 and Beilis. Then the Protocols: Znamya 1903, Ford's 91 parts, The Times's exposure in 1921, Mein Kampf and the first Arabic translation in 1925, Bern 1935, and their later use, including the Mufti's broadcasts and Hamas's 1988 charter. Figure: a timeline (at most 7 rows). Link forward to the Holocaust's documented scale [scene:hol_s05].

The word's own history, in order: Schlözer coins 'Semitic' for languages (1781); Renan turns it into a 'race' (1855); Steinschneider's first 'antisemitic', aimed at Renan (1860); Marr's League of Antisemites, aimed only at Jews (1879); Pinsker's 'Judeophobia' (1882); IHRA dropping the hyphen (2015). End with what the word means now: a misnomer at its root, settled in its meaning. Figure: a timeline of the six dates.

The menorah (Exodus; the Arch of Titus, 81 CE) against the Star of David (distinctively Jewish from 14th-century Prague), the 1897 Congress flag, and the 1948 decision to keep it, including the documented attempt to design a different flag and the emblem process. Keep 'what the choice encodes' and 'the programming' in a labeled interpretive passage. Figure: a timeline of the two symbols.

The word as a shield: the IHRA definition's own fine print, Kenneth Stern's criticism, its path from guideline into law (the executive order, 35 states, a House bill), what the label costs, and the chilling effect. Set out all three competing definitions from az_s01 and ihra_s02 (IHRA, with 7 of its 11 examples concerning Israel; the Jerusalem Declaration, with 200+ signatories; the Nexus Document), giving the strongest case for IHRA in its supporters' terms. State plainly that antisemitism is real and at record levels, with az_s01's incident figures, and use cmt_s09's verdict on the 'Free Palestine' claim. Close with the test (who is the target?). Figure: a comparison of the three definitions.

chapters.title: Peoples and Traditions
chapters.intro: The Jewish lineages and what the genetics shows, a thousand years of shared life in the Muslim world, the land's other communities, the difference between a religion and a political movement, the long record of dissent from within, and the Christian argument over one verse.

sections.brief: Mizrahi, Sephardi and Ashkenazi origins; Behar et al. 2010 (14 Jewish communities against 69 others) and the 2013 Khazar test, with kh_s01's 1,774 samples from 106 populations and the claim's antisemitic history; the documented, partial maternal European admixture; and the February 2026 revival. Add Beta Israel from et_s01 (Ovadia Yosef's ruling of 1973; the Law of Return applied in 1975), and state plainly that genetics settles no one's rights. Figure: a comparison of the three lineages. Link forward for the Jews of Iran [scene:ira_src_s16].

Coexistence without utopia. Start with Babylon's Jews from 586 BCE (irq_e01) and Baghdad's community; then Andalusian convivencia and Granada 1066; Spain's expulsion of 1492 and its 2015 citizenship offer (132,226 applicants), from wr_s02; and the Ottoman millet. Present the dispute between the 'golden age' and the 'persecution' readings fairly. Link to Faisal's Iraq rather than retelling it [scene:irq_e02]. Figure: a timeline from 586 BCE to 1492.

The land's other communities: the Druze (14,500 in 1949, about 150,000 today; conscripted 1956; courts 1961; the Golan Druze who refused citizenship); the Negev Bedouin (92,000 before 1948 and 11,000 after, the siyag, the 1953 and 1965 laws, seven townships, unrecognized villages and the Wadi al-Khalil demolitions of May 2024); the Circassians of Kfar Kama and Rehaniya; the Samaritans (146 in 1917, 654 in 2003); and Palestinian Christians, from about 12% to about 1%, with the 2025 Holy Family Church strike (pc_s03). Present both disputes: the village population figures, and squatters against a dispossessed people. Figure: key figures.

Zionism as a political movement founded at Basel in August 1897, and Judaism as a religion, with the distinction on one timeline. Cover Herzl in his own words (territorially agnostic at first), Reform Judaism's Pittsburgh Platform (1885), the Bund (October 1897), Ahad Ha'am's 'Truth from Eretz Israel' (1891) and Satmar's VaYoel Moshe (1958); then the Uganda/Argentina test of the accusation and the 'selective framing'. State the strongest Zionist case for Jewish peoplehood fairly. Link to the rabbinic debate over the Three Oaths [scene:oaths_s01] and to Basel [scene:s04].

Show that opposition to Zionism crosses every lineage: the Bund (and its dissolution by the Bolsheviks in 1921 and Liber's execution in 1937), Reform in 1885, Neturei Karta, the Mizrahi critique (Shohat, Chetrit, Shenhav), and the binationalists Buber, Magnes and Arendt (Brit Shalom 1925, Ihud 1942, testimony against partition, and why the project failed). Add today's numbers from gx_s04: the September 2025 Washington Post poll of 815 American Jews, with 61% saying war crimes and 76% saying Israel is vital. Present the case that these were minorities alongside the case that they were real currents. Figure: a timeline of the dissenting traditions.

Genesis 12:3 and the land promise (12:7, 15:18, 17:8); the Christian Zionist reading (ICEJ; dispensationalism); the covenant reading, fulfilled in Christ; and Cruz against Carlson (2025). From vat_s03, tell only the Scofield and dispensationalism question and why Rome never campaigned against it; from vat_s01, the Vatican's theological and political reasons for withholding recognition until 1993, told briefly and linked. Embed map christian_zionism. Link the Scofield Bible [scene:s05] and the Protestant restoration lobby [scene:bc_s05] rather than retelling them. Figure: a comparison of the two readings.

chapters.title: Two Displacements
chapters.intro: Two great movements of people in the middle of the twentieth century, the Jews of the Arab world and the Palestinians of 1948, each told on its own terms, and why they were not one even exchange.

sections.brief: The Jewish exodus from the Arab world, 1941–1972, and its several documented causes: the Farhud of 1–2 June 1941 (150–180+ killed; irq_e03), Iraq's criminalization of 'Zionism' (irq_e04), and Operation Ezra and Nehemiah (about 120,000–130,000; the denaturalization law; the disputed bombings; irq_e05), then Magic Carpet, Yachin, and the Lavon Affair (tell lv_s01 only as it touches Egypt's Jews, and link). Then arrival: the ma'abarot and unequal absorption, the Yemenite Children Affair (the 2001 commission against its dissenters) and the Ringworm Affair (an estimated 20,000–100,000+). Present the rescue reading and the recruitment-and-sabotage reading with their evidence. Figures: a timeline; key figures. Link forward to the 2021 Yemenite children decision [scene:mz_s02].

Country by country, with each figure's source: Libya (Giado; Tripoli, November 1945, 120 killed; 1948; 30,972 emigrants; the community's end), Egypt (75,000–80,000 in 1948; the 1948 bombs; the 1956 Suez measures and 25,000 departures), Aleppo, Aden (82 killed) and Bahrain after the partition vote, Yemen's airlift (ye_s01, nearly 50,000), Morocco's Operation Yachin (about 97,000, with payments; oa_s03), and Algeria (Crémieux citizenship; about 130,000 to France in 1962). Present the totals dispute (850,000 against Beker's 900,000) and the 'refugees' dispute (Beker against Shenhav and Amayreh, with the Stroum Center's middle line). Figure: a comparison table by country (departure years, main cause, main destination).

Test the 'even population exchange' claim on mechanism and timing: about 700,000–750,000 Palestinians displaced within one war of about 18 months, against a comparable but contested number of Jews over about 24 years, from many countries and for many causes. Cover the citizenship asymmetry (Israel naturalized the arrivals; Jordan naturalized most refugees, while Lebanon, Egypt and the Gulf did not; sq_s20), the regional aftermath from me_s07, and the rejection of the equivalence from both directions. Embed money_1948:Land & People:2 and discuss its ~700,000 (UN ~711,000) figure. Figure: a comparison of the two displacements. Link the Nakba's own story forward [scene:s10] and its historiography [scene:np_s01].

chapters.title: How the Story Is Told
chapters.intro: Who shapes what most people learn about this history: classrooms and textbooks, the historians and their arguments, state-funded and coordinated messaging, and the platforms' own rules, with the record running in both directions.

sections.brief: How the story is taught. Cover the K-12 textbook ('emphasis, not lies'), publisher self-certification and the cascade, the day-school curriculum and Birthright with their financial figures, the hasbara apparatus and the word's origin, Robert Maxwell (briefly; link [scene:s16]), the reflex the sequence installs, and the record. Hold the other side's curriculum to the same standard with sk_s05: the 2021 EU-commissioned study of about 200 Palestinian Authority textbooks and how each side reads it. Figures: a money chain for the return trip if its figures allow; a process flow of the textbook chain. Link to how Israel was sold to Americans in 1948 [scene:sell_s01].

How historians argue about 1948: the older account, the archives opened in the 1980s, Morris against Pappé on planning, Khalidi on Deir Yassin, Karsh and the other critics, and settler colonialism against national liberation as a framing dispute. Close with the discipline of reading the document first and then the interpreter. Figure: a comparison of the positions. Link forward [scene:np_s01] and [scene:pd_s01].

Coordination on the record. Cover STOIC (about $2 million, Israel's Diaspora Affairs Ministry), the Bridges Partners FARA filings, the leaked guidance chats, Netanyahu in the room, and the Israel on Campus Coalition takedown. Add Luntz's 2009 Global Language Dictionary (sk_s01) and the $150 million public-diplomacy budget of December 2024 with its FARA influencer contracts (inf_s01). Give the Iran-linked anti-Israel networks the same rigor. Figure: a money chain of state messaging funds.

Content moderation as a documented battlefield: HRW's 51-page report (1,050 cases) and Meta's own commissioned review; mt_s02 on '1,049 to 1' and what the dataset can and cannot show; Israel's Cyber Unit (9,500 requests in about six weeks, a reported 94% compliance; mt_s01); the TikTok figures (27% of 25,000+); and the post-Oracle case. Add from df_s11 what Meta's own policy text says about 'Zionist' as a proxy for a protected category, and who objected. Give the other direction equal weight: the ADL's findings on antisemitic content, TikTok's denial, the methodological critique of HRW, and the watermelon. State that neither the 'neutral platforms' story nor the 'conspiracy' story survives the full record. Figure: key figures; link to how the press coverage differed [scene:gx_s07].
